title: Passing off vs trademark infringement - the difference that matters
p1:
Two businesses can sell similar products and still face very different legal problems.

Many people think trademark infringement and passing off are the same thing. They are not.
p2:
The surprising part? A business can win a passing off claim even without owning a registered trademark.

Passing off protects the reputation you have built. It focuses on whether someone is misleading customers by making their product look connected to yours.
p3:
Trademark infringement is different. It usually happens when someone uses a registered trademark without permission, creating a legal violation based on the trademark itself.

A simple way to remember it:

Passing off protects your goodwill. Trademark infringement protects your registered brand identity.

For founders, this difference matters when deciding how to protect a brand before problems arise.
conclusion: Have you ever come across a brand that looked confusingly similar to another one? Would you consider it passing off, trademark infringement, or both?
